implementation_notes: Slick lifts the query into Scala: Table objects define the class/field-to-table/column mapping, Rep[T] wraps scalar expressions so queries are typed at the lifted level, and Query carries the collection methods (map/filter/flatMap/take/groupBy) that compile to a syntax tree rendered as SQL; sorting and filtering return a new Query of the same type, and filterOpt/filterIf express dynamic criteria from web forms. What replaces the classic query class is the lifted embedding plus implicit conversions; string SQL via StaticQuery stays justified for dialect-specific constructs the lifted API cannot express.
code_sketch:
val q = coffees.filter(_.supID === 101).sortBy(_.name)
val dynamic = coffees.filterOpt(optionFromPrice)(_.price > _)
dynamic.map(c => (c.name, c.price)).result   // DBIO; rendered per profile
pitfalls: Lifted expressions need ===/=!= and ++ (not ==/!= or +), otherwise Scala semantics silently replace SQL semantics.
Monadic joins (flatMap-based) that Slick cannot translate fail at runtime, not at compile time.
Queries are DBIO values bound to a profile: importing the wrong profile (H2 vs PostgreSQL) renders and executes against the wrong dialect.
